documents.title: Emergency department record (12/12/2021)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, community hospital
Seen 12/12/2021

CC: worst headache of life.

HPI: 58-year-old woman who, while out in her garden covering perennial beds around 11:45 today, had an instant, explosive headache, maximal at onset. Nauseated since, light hurts her eyes. No loss of consciousness, no seizure. Background of trigeminal neuralgia, Ramsay Hunt syndrome with facial nerve decompression, ovarian cancer in remission, RA on methotrexate and prednisone, hypertension, diabetes on insulin, hypothyroidism. NKDA. Mother had a subarachnoid hemorrhage at 68.

Triage: BP 165/95, HR 88.
Exam: awake and alert, anxious. GCS 15. Neck stiff, Brudzinski sign positive. Pupils equal and reactive. No focal motor or sensory deficit beyond chronic distal numbness; mild old right lower facial asymmetry.

CT head without contrast: diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage.
Cerebral angiography (neurointerventional, same afternoon): no aneurysm or vascular malformation identified.

Treatment: IV antiemetic, analgesia, nicardipine infusion for blood pressure, insulin per the admitting team.

Disposition: admitted to the neurointensive care unit under neurocritical care.

medications.sig: Take 2 capsules (60 mg) by mouth every 4 hours to complete 21 days (last dose 01/01/2022)

procedures.procedure: Endovascular coil embolization of anterior communicating artery aneurysm
Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (12/12/2021 - 12/28/2021)
documents.author: neurocritical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital, neurocritical care
Admitted 12/12/2021, discharged 12/28/2021

Diagnosis: subarachnoid hemorrhage from a ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm, initially angiographically occult.

Course: admitted to the neuro ICU after a negative first angiogram. Started nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days. Blood pressure controlled with a short nicardipine infusion, then her home lisinopril and HCTZ. Glucose managed on glargine with correction insulin; steroid continued at 5 mg. Methotrexate held while inpatient, resumed at discharge.
Repeat catheter angiography on 12/19 demonstrated a 4 mm anterior communicating artery aneurysm. Endovascular coil embolization on 12/20 with complete occlusion; no complications. Transcranial Dopplers monitored through day 14 without vasospasm requiring treatment. Headache steadily improved. Neurologic exam remained nonfocal.

Discharge exam: alert, oriented, fluent, full strength, steady gait.

Discharge medications: home regimen as before (lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, atorvastatin 40, levothyroxine 112 mcg, glargine 20 units, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, prednisone 5, carbamazepine 200 twice daily, ondansetron as needed) plus nimodipine through 01/01/2022. Acetaminophen for headache.

Follow-up: PCP within one week; neurointerventional clinic with catheter angiogram in 6 months; no driving for 4 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home since yesterday after aneurysm bleed and coiling. Headache mild, acetaminophen twice a day. No new weakness, speech normal. Has nimodipine through 1/1, taking every 4 hours including overnight alarms. A friend is driving her to appointments. Sugars 130s to 180s. Visit with PCP 1/4 confirmed. Med list reconciled against discharge summary, no discrepancies.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 1 week after discharge for aneurysmal SAH, AComm aneurysm coiled 12/20. Discharge summary reviewed in full.
Finished nimodipine on 1/1. Headache now a dull ache in the afternoons, acetaminophen once daily. Tired. No confusion, no weakness, no vision change, no seizure. Not driving until late January per neurosurgery.
She told me her mother had the same bleed at 68 and she had always wondered.
BP 128/78. Neuro: alert, oriented, fluent, cranial nerves intact apart from her old slight right smile asymmetry, strength full, gait steady.
A/P: SAH from ruptured AComm aneurysm, recovering well. Keep BP under 130/80, current lisinopril and HCTZ doing that. No smoking (she quit long ago). Avoid heavy lifting for a few weeks. Sodium checked on carbamazepine after hospitalization: today. 6-month angiogram is booked. Return in 10 weeks or sooner.
